Plastics Engineering Vs. The Presiding Officer, Labour Court-II< Chandigarh and another and lastly in Civil 
Appeal No.9792 ०2070 SC, Madhya Bharat Gramin Bank Vs. Panchal Yadav, decided on 73 July, 2027, 


0. The Hon’ble Apex Court in case of “Deepali Gundu Surwase v. Kranti Junion Adhyapak 
Mahavidyalaya” reported as (203) 0 SCC 324 has held as under:- 


“The propositions which can be culled out from the aforementioned judgments are: 


i) In cases of wrongful termination of service, reinstatement with continuity of service 
and back wages is the normal rule. 


ii) Ordinarily, an employee or workman whose services are terminated and who is 
desirous of getting back wages is required to either plead or at least make a statement 
before the adjudicating authority or the Court of first instance that he/she was not 
gainfully employed or was employed on lesser wages. If the employer wants to avoid 
payment of full back wages, then I has to plead and also lead cogent evidence to 
prove that the employee/workman was gainfully employed and was getting wages 
equal to the wages he/she was drawing prior to the termination of service. This is so 
because it is settled law that the burden of proof of the existence of a particular fact 
lies on the person who makes a positive averments about its existence. It is always 
easier to prove a positive fact than to prove a negative fact. Therefore, once the 
employee shows that he was employed, the onus lies on the employer to specifically 
plead and prove that the employee was gainfully employed and was getting the same 
or substantially similar emoluments.” 


ll. Hon’ble Apex Court in the case General Manager, Haryana Roadways Vs. Rudan Singh, reported as 2005 
SCC (L & S) 776 observed as under:- 


“There is no rule of thumb that in every case where the Industrial Tribunal gives a 
finding that the termination of service was in violation of Section 25-F of the Act, entire back 
wages should be awarded. A host of factors like the manner and method of selection and 
appointment i.e. whether after proper advertisement of the vacancy or inviting applications 
from the employment exchange, nature of appointment namely, whether ad hoc, short term, 
daily wage, temporary or permanent in character, any special qualification required for the job 
and the like should be weighed and balanced in taking a decision regarding award of back 
wages. One of the important factors which has to be taken into consideration is the length of 
service, which the workman had rendered with the employer. If the workman has rendered a 
considerable period of service and his services are wrongfully terminated, he may be 
awarded full or partial back wages keeping in view the fact that at this age and the 
qualification possessed by him he may not be in a position to get another employment. 
However, where the total length of service rendered by a workman is very small, the award of 
back wages for the complete period i.e. from the date of termination till the date of the award, 
which our experience shows is often quite large, would be wholly inappropriate. A regular 
service of permanent character cannot be compared to short or intermittent daily wage 
employment though it may be for 240 days in a calendar year.” 


296 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : APRIL 29, 2023/ VAISAKHA 9, [945 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


2. The Hon’ble Apex Court while considering the violation of Section 25-F of the Act in Incharge Officer & 
Anr. V. Shankar Shetty, (2070) 9 SCC 726: 2070 LLR 737 and after referring to the various decisions, held that the 
relief by way of back wages is not automatic and compensation instead of reinstatement has been held to meet the 
ends of justice and it was observed as under: - 


“2. Should an order of reinstatement automatically follow in a case where the 
engagement of a daily wager has been brought to end in violation of Section 25F of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 79476छ short “the ID Act”)? The course of the decisions of this Court 
in recent years has been uniform on the above question. 


3. In Jagbir Singh V. Haryana State Agriculture Mktg. Board, (2009) 75 SCC 327, 
delivering the judgment of this Court, one of the us (R.M. Lodha, J.) noticed some of the recent 
decisions of this Court, namely, U.P. State Brassware Corpn. Ltd. V. Uday Narain Pandey, 
(2006) I SCC 479; Uttaranchal Forest Development Corpn. V. M.C. Joshi, (2007) 9 SCC 353; 
State of M.P. v. Lalit Kumar Verma, (2007) I SCC 575; M.P. Admn. V. Tribhuban, (2007) 9 
SCC 748; Sita Ram v. Moti Lal Nehru Farmers Training Institute, (2008)5 SCC 75; Jaipur 
Development Authority v. Ramsahai, (2006) 77 SCC 684; GDA v. Ashok Kumar, (2008) 4 SCC 
267 and Mahboob Deepak v. Nagar Panchayat, Gajraula, (2008) I SCC 575 and stated as 
follows: (Jagbir Singh case (2009) 77 SCC 327, SCC pp. 330 & 335, paras 7 & 74) 


“7, It is true that the earlier view of this Court articulated in many decisions reflected the 
legal position that if the termination of an employee was found to be illegal, the relief of 
reinstatement with full back-wages would ordinarily follow. However, in recent past, there has 
been a shift in the legal position and in a long line of cases, this Court has consistently taken 
the view that relief by way of reinstatement with back-wages is not automatic and may be wholly 
inappropriate in a given fact situation even though the termination of an employee is in 
contravention of the prescribed procedure. Compensation instead of reinstatement has been 
held to meet the ends of justice. 


34, It would be, thus, seen that by a catena of decisions in recent time, this Court has 
clearly laid down that an order of retrenchment passed in violation of Section 25F although 
may be set aside but an award of reinstatement should not, however, be automatically passed.” 


3. The workman has alleged in his claim statement that he worked as messenger with the management from 
0.06.2009 to 02.08.203 and was getting Rs.4,500/- per month. The name of the workman was also recommended 
by the Branch Manager, AG Sudhar Branch-087 vide his letter Ref. No.340/20! dated 27.05.20i] and the name of 
the workman was also forwarded by the respondents (Regional Office for registering his name under staff son 
category vide letter No.RO/ST/4I/99 dated 25.08.99. The workman was called for interview vide letter 
No. RO/PAD/I/203-4 dated 05.06.20!3 before the Regional Office Fountain Chowk, College Road, Civil Lines, 
Ludhiana on 24.06.203 at 9.00 AM. The workman served the legal notice through his counsel on 26.07.203 for the 
said attitude of the management. The management sent frivolous reply through his counsel vide reply dated 
3.08.203 taking false plea. The juniors to the workman were retained in service. The workman was completed 240 
days of work in the preceding year from the date of his termination. 


4. In view of legal position discussed above, this Court is of the considered view that workman herein was not 
holding a regular or permanent post nor he was recruited against the post is a regular manner. In such circumstances, 
it is appropriate to grant reasonable compensation instead of reinstatement with back wages. 

5. As such, having due regard to the facts and circumstances, an amount of Rs.50,000/-(Fifty Thousand) 
appears to be just and reasonable to which the workman is entitled. In case, the amount of Rs.50,000/-(Fifty 
Thousand) not paid within one month from the date of publication of the award, the workman is held to be entitled to 
6% interest from the date of reference till payment. File after completion be consigned in the record room. 

6. Let copy of this award be sent to Central Government for publication as required under Section |7 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 947.

MINISTRY OF DEFENCE 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 17th April, 2023 


S.R.O. 66.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Indian Air Force, Library and Information Assistant (Group ‘C’ posts) Recruitment Rule, 1994, 
except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the 
following rules regulating the method of recruitment for the post of Library and Information Assistant, namely: - 


1. Short title and commencement.-(1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Defence, Indian Air Force, 
Library and Information Assistant, Group ‘B’ Post, Recruitment Rules, 2023. 

(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 
2: Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix.-The number of the said post, its classification and 


level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these 
rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age limit, qualifications, etc The method of recruitment to the said post, age- 
limit, educational qualifications and other matters relating thereto shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the 
said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification .-No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said posts: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax.- Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving.-Nothing in these rules shall affect reservations, relaxation of the age limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Schedule Castes, the Schedule Tribes, Ex-servicemen and other special categories of 
persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in the regard.

New Delhi, the 17th April, 2023 
S.R.O. 67.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, and in 
supersession of the Indian Air Force Civilian Gazetted Officer (Equipment) Recruitment Rules, 2004, except as 


respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules 
regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Civilian Gazetted Officer (Equipment) in the Indian Air Force, 


namely:- 
1. Short title and commencement — (1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Defence, Indian Air Force, 
Civilian Gazetted Officer (Equipment) Recruitment Rules, 2023. 

(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix—The number of the said post, its classification and 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these 
rules. 
3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc —The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications 


and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification No person ,- 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 


Shall be eligible for appointment to the said posts: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax.—Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order, and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons.

Patel National Police Academy, Hyderabad in the Ministry of Home Affairs, namely :-

G.S.R. 46.— In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Regional Leprosy Training and Research Institute, Raipur (Pharmacist), Non-gazetted post, 
Recruitment Rules, 2002, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President 
hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Pharmacist (Group ‘C’ post) in 
the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Regional Leprosy Training and Research Institute, Raipur namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement.-(1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 
Regional Leprosy Training and Research Institute, Raipur, Pharmacist (Group 'C’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 2023. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix.- The number of said post, its classification and level in 
the pay matrix attached thereto, shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualification, etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. - No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, 
by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class 
or category of persons. 


6. Saving. - Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to be 
provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the Ex-servicemen or any other 
special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in this 
regard.

G.S.R. 47.— In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, and in 
supersession of the General Leprosy Training Research Institute, (Group D Posts) Recruitment Rules, 1978, in so far 
it relates to the post of Laboratory Attendant, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such 
supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment for the post 
of Laboratory Attendant in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Central Leprosy Teaching and Research 
Institute, Chengalpattu, namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 
Central Leprosy Teaching and Research Institute, Chengalpattu, Laboratory Attendant (Group ‘C‘ Post) Recruitment 
Rules, 2023. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix. - The number of said post, its classification and level in 
pay matrix attached thereto, shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. - No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person; 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law 
applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt any 
person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient to do so, it may, 
by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class 
or category of persons. 


6. Saving.- Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to be 
provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the Ex-servicemen and other

G.S.R. 49.— In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution 
and in supersession of the Central Leprosy Training and Research Institute, Chengalpattu (Cobbler Grade-II) 
Recruitment Rules, 2001, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President 
hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Cobbler Grade II in the Ministry 
of Health and Family Welfare, Central Leprosy Teaching and Research Institute, Chengalpattu, namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare , 
Central Leprosy Teaching and Research Institute, Chengalpattu, Cobbler Grade II (Group ‘C' Post) Recruitment 
Rules, 2023. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix.- The number of the said post, its classification and level 
in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. - No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, 
by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class 
or category of persons. 


6. Saving. - Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to be 
provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the Ex-servicemen and other 
special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in this 
regard.

ELECTION COMMISSION OF INDIA 
ORDER 
New Delhi, the 8th February, 2023 


0.४ 52.—WHEREAS, WHEREAS, the General Election to 202-Bidhuna Legislative Assembly of 
Uttarpradesh, 2022 was announced vide Notification No. 60/61-2022 dated 25" January, 2022. 


AND,WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate 
at an election has to, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge a true copy of the 
account of his election expenses with the District Election Officer; 


AND,WHEREAS, the result of the said election along with 202-Bidhuna Assembly Constituency was 
declared by the concerned Returning Officer on 107 March, 2022. Hence, the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 09" April, 2022; 


AND WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Auraiya, Uttarpradesh and 
forwarded by the Joint Chief Electoral Officer, Uttarpradesh vide their letter No. 287/Nirvachan Vayy Cell/GE- 
LA/2022/Patra-01/2021, dated 27" April, 2021, Er. Shivam Pal a contesting candidate of Uttarpradesh from 202- 
Bidhuna Assembly Constituency of Uttarpradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election expenses, in the manner, 
as required under law; 


AND WHEREAS, on the basis of the reports of the District Election Officer, Auraiya, Uttarpradesh and the 
Chief Electoral Officer, Uttarpradesh, a Show-Cause notice, 76/UP-LA/2022/CEMS-III dated 11.11.2022 was issued 
under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Er. 
Shivam Pal for not lodging the account of Election Expenses; 


AND WHEREAS, As per the sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, through the 
above said Show-Cause Notice, dated 11.11.2022, Er. Shivam Pal was directed to submit his representation in 
writing with explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and to lodge account of election expenses within 20 
days from the date of receipt of the notice; 


AND WHEREAS, the said notice was received by Shri Rinku Pal brother of the candidate on 07.12.2022. The 
acknowledgment receipt has been submitted to the Commission by the District Election Officer, Auraiya, vide its 
letter no. 1878/DEO-29/Nirva. Vayycell/2022; 


AND WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Auraiya, in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter No. 
1878/DEO-29/Nirva.Vayycell/2022 dated 31.12.2022 has reported that Er. Shivam Pal has neither submitted any 
representation nor any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the due notice of the 
Election Commission of India, he has furnished neither any reason nor explanation for the said failure; 


AND WHEREAS, the Commission is satisfied that Er. Shivam Pal has failed to lodge the account of election 
expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


AND WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: - 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


i. has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or 
under this Act, and 


il. has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order’’; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Er. Shivam Pal resident of House No. 54, Parshuram Gali, 
Lohiyanagar, Dibiyapur, Auraiya a contesting candidate from 202-Bidhuna, Assembly Constituency of the State of 
Uttarpradesh in the General Election to the Legislative Assembly 2022 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for 
being a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or 
Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

New Delhi, the 8th February, 2023 


O.N. 53.— WHEREAS, the General Election to 202-Bidhuna Legislative Assembly of Uttarpradesh, 2022 
was announced vide Notification No. 60/61-2022 dated 25" January, 2022. 


AND,WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate 
at an election has to, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge a true copy of the 
account of his election expenses with the District Election Officer; 


AND,WHEREAS, the result of the said election along with 202-Bidhuna Assembly Constituency was 
declared by the concerned Returning Officer on 10" March, 2022. Hence, the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 09" April, 2022; 


AND WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Auraiya, Uttarpradesh and 
forwarded by the Joint Chief Electoral Officer, Uttarpradesh vide their letter No. 287/Nirvachan Vayy Cell/GE- 
LA/2022/Patra-01/2021, dated 27" April, 2021, Shri Gaurav Raghuvanshi a contesting candidate of Uttarpradesh 
from 202-Bidhuna Assembly Constituency of Uttarpradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election expenses, in 
the manner, as required under law; 


AND WHEREAS, on the basis of the reports of the District Election Officer, Auraiya, Uttarpradesh and the 
Chief Electoral Officer, Uttarpradesh, a Show-Cause notice, 76/UP-LA/2022/CEMS-III dated 11.11.2022 was issued 
under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Shri 
Gaurav Raghuvanshi for not lodging the account of Election Expenses; 


AND WHEREAS, As per the sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, through the 
above said Show-Cause Notice, dated 11.11.2022, Shri Gaurav Raghuvanshi was directed to submit his 
representation in writing with explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and to lodge account of election 
expenses within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; 


AND WHEREAS, the said notice was received by Shri Dhrampal singh father of the candidate on 04.12.2022. 
The acknowledgment receipt has been submitted to the Commission by the District Election Officer, Auraiya, vide its 
letter no. 1878/DEO-29/Nirva. Vayycell/2022; 


AND WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Auraiya, in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter No. 
1878/DEO-29/Nirva.Vayycell/2022 dated 31.12.2022 has reported that Shri Gaurav Raghuvanshi has neither 
submitted any representation nor any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the due notice 
of the Election Commission of India, he has furnished neither any reason nor explanation for the said failure; 


AND WHEREAS, the Commission is satisfied that Shri Gaurav Raghuvanshi has failed to lodge the 
account of election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


124 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 6, 2023/VAISAKHA 16, 1945 [PART II—SEC. 3(iii)] 


AND WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: - 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


i. has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or 
under this Act, and 


il. has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order”’; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Shri Gaurav Raghuvanshi resident of Vill - Rampura Mauja 
Umrain, Tehsil - Bidhuna, Auraiya a contesting candidate from 202-Bidhuna, Assembly Constituency of the State 
of Uttarpradesh in the General Election to the Legislative Assembly 2022 to be disqualified for being chosen as and 
for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a 
State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

O.N. 55.— WHEREAS, the General Election to 259-Meja Legislative Assembly of Uttar Pradesh, 2022 was 
announced vide Notification No. 86/61-2022 dated 01“ February, 2022. 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election has to, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge a true copy of the account of 
his election expenses with the District Election Officer; and, 


WHEREAS, the result of the said election along with 259-Meja Assembly Constituency was declared by the 
concerned Returning Officer on 107 March, 2022. Hence, the last date for lodging the account of Election Expenses 
was 097 April, 2022; and, 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh and 
forwarded by the Joint Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh vide their letter No. 287/Nirvachan Vayy Cell/GE- 
LA/2022/Patra-01/2021, dated 27" April, 2021, Shri Vivekanand a contesting candidate of Uttar Pradesh from 
259-Meja Assembly Constituency of Uttar Pradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election expenses, in the 
manner, as required under law; and, 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the reports of the District Election Officer, Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh and the 
Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, a Show-Cause notice, 76/UP-LA/2022/CEMS-III dated 14.11.2022 was issued 
under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to 
Shri Vivekanand for not lodging the account of Election Expenses; and, 


WHEREAS, As per the sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, through the above 
said Show-Cause Notice, dated 14.11.2022, Shri Vivekanand was directed to submit his representation in writing 
with explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and to lodge account of election expenses within 20 days from 
the date of receipt of the notice; and, 


WHEREAS, the said notice was pasted at address given by the candidate on 07.12.2022. The acknowledgment 
receipt has been submitted to the Commission by the District Election Officer, Prayagraj, vide its letter no. 1254/29- 
Vidhansabha Nirvachan-2022; and, 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Prayagraj in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter 
No. 1254/29-Vidhansabha Nirvachan-2022 dated 05.01.2023 has reported that Shri Vivekanand has neither 
submitted any representation nor any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the due notice 
of the Election Commission of India, he has furnished neither any reason nor explanation for the said failure; and, 


WHEREAS, the Commission is satisfied that Shri Vivekanand has failed to lodge the account of election 
expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


i. has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or 
under this Act, and 


ii. has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order”; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Shri Vivekanand resident of Village - Bhringari, Post-Dohariya, 
District- Prayagraj a contesting candidate from 259-Meja Assembly Constituency of the State of Uttar Pradesh in 
the General Election to the Legislative Assembly 2022 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member 
of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory 
for a period of three years from the date of this order.

O.N. 57.—WHEREAS, the General Election to 296-Gonda Legislative Assembly of Uttar Pradesh, 2022 
was announced vide Notification No. 86/61-2022 dated 1“ February, 2022. 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election has to, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge a true copy of the account of 
his election expenses with the District Election Officer; and, 


WHEREAS, the result of the said election along with 296-Gonda Assembly Constituency was declared by the 
concerned Returning Officer on 107 March, 2022. Hence, the last date for lodging the account of Election Expenses 
was 097 April, 2022; and, 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Gonda, Uttar Pradesh and forwarded 
by the Joint Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh vide their letter No. 287/Nirvachan Vayy Cell/GE-LA/2022/Patra- 
01/2021, dated 27" April, 2021, Sundari Pandey a contesting candidate of UttarP radesh from 296-Gonda Assembly 
Constituency of Uttar Pradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election expenses, in the manner, as required under 
law; and, 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the reports of the District Election Officer, Gonda, Uttar Pradesh and the Chief 
Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, a Show-Cause notice, 76/UP-LA/2022/CEMS-III dated 13.12.2022 was issued under 
sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to 
Sundari Pandey for not lodging the account of Election Expenses; and,

WHEREAS, As per the sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, through the above 
said Show-Cause Notice, dated 13.12.2022, Sundari Pandey was directed to submit his representation in writing with 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and to lodge account of election expenses within 20 days from the 
date of receipt of the notice; and, 


WHEREAS, the said notice was received by the candidate on 04.01.2023. The acknowledgment receipt has 


been submitted to the Commission by the District Election Officer, Gonda, vide its letter No. 65/निर्वाचन/वि.स.सा.नि.- 
2022-23; and, 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Gonda in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter No. 108/ 
निर्वाचन/वि.स.सा.नि.-2022-23 dated 28.01.2023 has reported that Sundari Pandey has neither submitted any 
representation nor any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the due notice of the 
Election Commission of India, he has furnished neither any reason nor explanation for the said failure; and, 


WHEREAS, the Commission is satisfied that Sundari Pandey has failed to lodge the account of election 
expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


i. has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or 
under this Act, and 


ii. has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order”; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sundari Pandey resident of Village Sisai Tikriya, Post Vishunpur, 
District Gonda a contesting candidate from 296-Gonda Assembly Constituency of the State of Uttar Pradesh in the 
General Election to the Legislative Assembly 2022 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of 
either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for 
a period of three years from the date of this order.

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 21st February, 2023 


O.N. 58.—WHEREAS, the General Election to 299-Tarabganj Legislative Assembly of Uttar Pradesh, 2022 
was announced vide Notification No. 86/61-2022 dated 1“ February, 2022. 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election has to, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge a true copy of the account of 
his election expenses with the District Election Officer; and, 


WHEREAS, the result of the said election along with 299-Tarabganj Assembly Constituency was declared 
by the concerned Returning Officer on 107 March, 2022. Hence, the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 097 April, 2022; and, 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Gonda, Uttar Pradesh and forwarded 
by the Joint Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh vide their letter No. 287/Nirvachan Vayy Cell/GE-LA/2022/Patra- 
01/2021, dated 27" April, 2021, Jaswant Singh a contesting candidate of Uttar Pradesh from 299-Tarabganj 
Assembly Constituency of Uttar Pradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election expenses, in the manner, as 
required under law; and, 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the reports of the District Election Officer, Gonda, Uttar Pradesh and the Chief 
Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, a Show-Cause notice, 76/UP-LA/2022/CEMS-III dated 13.12.2022 was issued under 
sub-rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Jaswant 
Singh for not lodging the account of Election Expenses; and, 


WHEREAS, As per the sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, through the above 
said Show-Cause Notice, dated 13.12.2022, Jaswant Singh was directed to submit his representation in writing with 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and to lodge account of election expenses within 20 days from the 
date of receipt of the notice; and, 


WHEREAS, the said notice was received by Shri Rakesh Kumar Singh brother of the candidate on 
03.01.2023. The acknowledgment receipt has been submitted to the Commission by the District Election Officer, 


Gonda, vide its letter No. 65/निर्वाचन/वि.स.सा.नि.-2022-23; and, 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Gonda in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter No. 108/ 
निर्वाचन/वि.स.सा.नि.-2022-23 dated 28.01.2023 has reported that Jaswant Singh has neither submitted any 
representation nor any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the due notice of the 
Election Commission of India, he has furnished neither any reason nor explanation for the said failure; and, 


WHEREAS, the Commission is satisfied that Jaswant Singh has failed to lodge the account of election 
expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


i. has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or 
under this Act, and 


ii. has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order”; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Jaswant Singh resident of Village-Muher, Post-Belsar, District 
Gonda a contesting candidate from 299-Tarabganj Assembly Constituency of the State of Uttar Pradesh in the 
General Election to the Legislative Assembly 2022 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of 
either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for 
a period of three years from the date of this order. 


[No. 76/UP-LA/Gonda/2022/CEMS--IIT] 
By Order, 
BINOD KUMAR, Secy.

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 21st February, 2023 


O.N. 60.—WHEREAS, the General Election to 299-Tarabganj Legislative Assembly of Uttar Pradesh, 
2022 was announced vide Notification No. 86/61-2022 dated 1* February, 2022. 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at 
an election has to, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge a true copy of the account 
of his election expenses with the District Election Officer; and, 


WHEREAS, the result of the said election along with 299-Tarabganj Assembly Constituency was declared 
by the concerned Returning Officer on 107 March, 2022. Hence, the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 097 April, 2022; and, 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Gonda, Uttar Pradesh and 
forwarded by the Joint Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh vide their letter No. 287/Nirvachan Vayy Cell/GE- 
LA/2022/Patra-01/2021, dated 27" April, 2021, Om Prakash a contesting candidate of Uttar Pradesh from 299- 
Tarabganj Assembly Constituency of Uttar Pradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election expenses, in the 
manner, as required under law; and, 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the reports of the District Election Officer, Gonda, Uttar Pradesh and the Chief 
Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, a Show-Cause notice, 76/UP-LA/2022/CEMS-III dated 13.12.2022 was issued under 
sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Om Prakash 
for not lodging the account of Election Expenses; and, 


WHEREAS, As per the sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, through the above 
said Show-Cause Notice, dated 13.12.2022, Om Prakash was directed to submit his representation in writing with 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and to lodge account of election expenses within 20 days from the 
date of receipt of the notice; and, 


140 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA: MAY 6, 2023/VAISAKHA 16, 1945 [PART II—SEC. 3(iii)] 


WHEREAS, the said notice was received by the candidate on 03.01.2023. The acknowledgment receipt has 
been submitted to the Commission by the District Election Officer, Gonda, vide its letter no. 65/निर्वाचन/वि.स.सा.नि.- 
2022-23; and, 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Gonda in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter No. 108/ 
निर्वाचन/वि.स.सा.नि.-2022-23 dated 28.01.2023 has reported that Om Prakash has neither submitted any 
representation nor any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the due notice of the 
Election Commission of India, he has furnished neither any reason nor explanation for the said failure; and, 


WHEREAS, the Commission is satisfied that Om Prakash has failed to lodge the account of election 
expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


i. has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or 
under this Act, and 


ii. has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order”; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Om Prakash resident of Village and Post -Niyawa, Thana- 
Tarabganj, District - Gonda a contesting candidate from 299-Tarabganj Assembly Constituency of the State of 
Uttar Pradesh in the General Election to the Legislative Assembly 2022 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for 
being a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or 
Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at 
an election has to, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge a true copy of the account 
of his election expenses with the District Election Officer; and, 


WHEREAS, the result of the said election along with 301-Gaura Assembly Constituency was declared by 
the concerned Returning Officer on 107 March, 2022. Hence, the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 097 April, 2022; and, 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Gonda, Uttar Pradesh and 
forwarded by the Joint Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh vide their letter No. 287/Nirvachan Vayy Cell/GE- 
LA/2022/Patra-01/2021, dated 27" April, 2021, Shyam Narayan a contesting candidate of Uttar Pradesh from 301- 
Gaura Assembly Constituency of Uttar Pradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election expenses, in the manner, 
as required under law; and, 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the reports of the District Election Officer, Gonda, Uttar Pradesh and the Chief 
Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, a Show-Cause notice, 76/UP-LA/2022/CEMS-III dated 13.12.2022 was issued under 
sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Shyam 
Narayan for not lodging the account of Election Expenses; and, 


WHEREAS, As per the sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, through the above 
said Show-Cause Notice, dated 13.12.2022 Shyam Narayan was directed to submit his representation in writing with 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and to lodge account of election expenses within 20 days from the 
date of receipt of the notice; and, 

WHEREAS, the said notice was received by the candidate on 24.12.2022. The acknowledgment receipt has 
been submitted to the Commission by the District Election Officer, Gonda, vide its letter no. 65/निर्वाचन/वि.स.सा.नि.- 
2022-23; and, 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Gonda in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter No. 108/ 
निर्वाचन/वि.स.सा.नि.-2022-23 dated 28.01.2023 has reported that Shyam Narayan has neither submitted any 
representation nor any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the due notice of the 
Election Commission of India, he has furnished neither any reason nor explanation for the said failure; and, 


WHEREAS, the Commission is satisfied that Shyam Narayan has failed to lodge the account of election 
expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


i. has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


ii. has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order”; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Shyam Narayan resident of Village -Naraicha, Post Swami Narayan 
Chapiya, District - Gonda a contesting candidate from 301-Gaura Assembly Constituency of the State of Uttar 
Pradesh in the General Election to the Legislative Assembly 2022 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being 
a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or 
Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order. 


[No. 76/UP-LA/Gonda/2022/CEMS -IIT] 
By Order, 
BINOD KUMAR, Secy.

आ.अ. 62.--यतः, उत्तर प्रदेश राज्य की 191-कादीपुर(अ.जा.) विधान सभा क्षेत्र के साधारण निर्वाचन 2022 की 
घोषणा अधिसूचना नं. 86/61-2022 दिनांक 01.02.2022 के जरिए की गई थी। 


यतः लोक प्रतिनिधित्व अधिनियम, 1951 की धारा 78 के अनुसार, निर्वाचन लड़ने वाले प्रत्येक अभ्यर्थी को, 
निर्वाचित अभ्यर्थी के निर्वाचन की तारीख से 30 दिनों के भीतर निर्वाचन व्यय के अपने लेखे की सही प्रति जिला निर्वाचन 
अधिकारी को दाखिल करनी होती है; और 

यतः 191-कादीपुर(अ.जा.) विधान सभा निर्वाचन क्षेत्र के रिटर्निंग अधिकारी द्वारा उक्त निर्वाचन का परिणाम 
10 मार्च, 2022 को घोषित किया गया था। इस प्रकार, निर्वाचन व्यय का लेखा दाखिल करने की अन्तिम तारीख 09 
अप्रैल, 2022 थी; और 


यतः, जिला निर्वाचन अधिकारी, सुलतानपुर, उत्तर प्रदेश के द्वारा प्रस्तुत और संयुक्त मुख्य निर्वाचन अधिकारी, 
उत्तर प्रदेश द्वारा पत्र सं. 287/निर्वाचन व्यय सेल/वि.स.सा.नि.-2022/पत्रा.-01/2021 के जरिए अग्रेषित दिनांक 
27/04/2022 की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार श्री धर्मेन्द्र कुमार जो उत्तर प्रदेश विधान सभा का साधारण निर्वाचन 2022 के 
निर्वाचन क्षेत्र 191-कादीपुर(अ.जा.) से लड़ने वाले अभ्यर्थी हैं, विधि द्वारा यथापेक्षित रीति से अपने निर्वाचन व्यय का कोई 
भी लेखा दाखिल करने में विफल रहे हैं; और, 


यतः, जिला निर्वाचन अधिकारी, सुलतानपुर, उत्तर प्रदेश, और मुख्य निर्वाचन अधिकारी, उत्तर प्रदेश की उक्त 
रिपोर्टों के आधार पर भारत निर्वाचन आयोग द्वारा निर्वाचनों का संचालन नियम 1961 के नियम 89 के उप नियम (5) के 
अंतर्गत निर्वाचन व्यय प्रस्तुत नहीं करने के लिए श्री धर्मेन्द्र कुमार को कारण बताओ नोटिस सं. 76/उत्तर प्रदेश- 
वि.स./2022/सी.ई.एम.एस.-|॥, दिनांक 01 दिसम्बर, 2022 जारी किया गया था; और 

यतः, निर्वाचनों का संचालन नियम 1961 के नियम 89 के उप-नियम (6) के अनुसार, दिनांक 01 दिसम्बर, 
2022 के उपर्युक्त कारण बताओ नोटिस के जरिए श्री धर्मेन्द्र कुमार को निदेश दिया गया था कि वे इस नोटिस के प्राप्त होने 
के 20 दिनों के अंदर लेखा न प्रस्तुत कर पाने के कारणों को स्पष्ट करते हुए लिखित रूप में अपना अभ्यावेदन प्रस्तुत करें 
और साथ ही, निर्वाचन व्यय का अपना लेखा दाखिल करें; और 

यतः, जिला निर्वाचन अधिकारी, सुलतानपुर द्वारा अपने दिनांक 27.12.2022 के पत्र संख्या 524/निर्वाचन 
(व्यय लेखा/वि.स.सा.-2022) के जरिए आयोग को सूचना दी गई की उक्त नोटिस अभ्यर्थी के द्वारा दिनांक 15.12.2022 
को प्राप्त किया गया था; और, 

यतः, जिला निर्वाचन अधिकारी, सुलतानपुर द्वारा दिनांक 08.02.2023 के पत्र संख्या 52/निर्वाचन(व्यय 
लेखा/वि.स.सा.-2022) के जरिए प्रस्तुत की गई अनुपूरक संवीक्षा रिपोर्ट में यह बताया गया है कि श्री धर्मेन्द्र कुमार ने न 
तो कोई भी अभ्यावेदन और न ही अपने निर्वाचन व्यय का लेखा दाखिल किया है। इसके अतिरिक्त उन्होंने भारत निर्वाचन 
आयोग का सम्यक्‌ नोटिस मिलने के उपरांत भी उक्त विफलता के लिए न तो कोई कारण बताया है और न ही कोई 
स्पष्टीकरण दिया है; और, 

यतः, आयोग का यह समाधान हो गया है कि श्री धर्मेन्द्र कुमार निर्वाचन खर्चों का लेखा दाखिल करने में विफल 
रहे हैं और उनके पास इस विफलता के लिए कोई भी उचितकारण अथवा औचित्य नहीं है; और 


यत:, लोक प्रतिनिधित्व अधिनियम, 1951 की धारा 10क में अनुबंधित किया गया है कि:- 
"यदि निर्वाचन आयोग का समाधान हो जाता है कि कोई व्यक्ति - 


i. निर्वाचन व्ययों का लेखा उस समय के भीतर और उस रीति में जैसी इस अधिनियम के द्वारा या अधीन अपेक्षित है, 
दाखिल करने में असफल रहा है; तथा

O.N. 62.—WHEREAS, the General Election to 191-Kadipur(SC) Legislative Assembly of Uttar Pradesh, 
2022 was announced vide Notification No. 86/61-2022 dated 1* February, 2022. 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at 
an election has to, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge a true copy of the account 
of his election expenses with the District Election Officer; and, 


WHEREAS, the result of the said election along with 191-Kadipur(SC) Assembly Constituency was 
declared by the concerned Returning Officer on 107 March, 2022. Hence, the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 097 April, 2022; and, 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh and 
forwarded by the Joint Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh vide their letter No. 287/Nirvachan Vayy Cell/GE- 
LA/2022/Patra-01/2021, dated 27" April, 2021, Shri Dharmendra Kumar a contesting candidate of Uttar Pradesh 
from 191-Kadipur(SC) Assembly Constituency of Uttar Pradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election expenses, 
in the manner, as required under law; and, 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the reports of the District Election Officer, Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh and the 
Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, a Show-Cause notice, 76/UP-LA/2022/CEMS-III dated 01.12.2022 was issued 
under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Shri 
Dharmendra Kumar for not lodging the account of Election Expenses; and, 


WHEREAS, As per the sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, through the above 
said Show-Cause Notice, dated 01.12.2022, Shri Dharmendra Kumar was directed to submit his representation in 
writing with explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and to lodge account of election expenses within 20 
days from the date of receipt of the notice; and, 


WHEREAS, the said notice was received by the candidate on 15.12.2022. The acknowledgment receipt has 
been submitted to the Commission by the District Election Officer, Sultanpur, vide its letter no. 524/निर्वाचन(व्यय 
लेखा/वि.स.सा.-2022); and, 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Sultanpur in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter No. 
52/निर्वाचन(व्यय लेखा/वि.स.सा.-2022) dated 08.02.2023 has reported that Shri Dharmendra Kumar has neither 


submitted any representation nor any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the due notice 
of the Election Commission of India, he has furnished neither any reason nor explanation for the said failure; and, 


WHEREAS, the Commission is satisfied that Shri Dharmendra Kumar has failed to lodge the account of 
election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 


“Tf the Election Commission is satisfied that a person-

i. has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


ii. has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order”; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Shri Dharmendra Kumar resident of Village-Baramadpur, Post- 
Makhdoo Baramadpur, District Sultanpur a contesting candidate from 191-Kadipur(SC) Assembly Constituency 
of the State of Uttar Pradesh in the General Election to the Legislative Assembly 2022 to be disqualified for being 
chosen as and for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative 
Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 2nd March, 2023 


O.N. 63.—WHEREAS, the General Election to 25-Kanth Legislative Assembly of Uttar Pradesh, 2022 was 
announced vide Notification No. 48/61-2022 dated 21" January, 2022. 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at 
an election has to, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge a true copy of the account 
of his election expenses with the District Election Officer; and, 


WHEREAS, the result of the said election along with 25-Kanth Assembly Constituency was declared by the 
concerned Returning Officer on 107 March, 2022. Hence, the last date for lodging the account of Election Expenses 
was 097 April, 2022; and, 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh and 
forwarded by the Joint Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh vide their letter No. 287/Nirvachan Vayy Cell/GE- 
LA/2022/Patra-01/2021, dated 27" April, 2021, Mohd Israr, a contesting candidate of Uttar Pradesh from 25-Kanth 
Assembly Constituency of Uttar Pradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election expenses, in the manner, as 
required under law; and, 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the reports of the District Election Officer Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh and the 
Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, a Show-Cause notice, 76/UP-LA/2022/CEMS-III dated 20.10.2022 was issued 
under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to 
Mohd Israr for not lodging the account of Election Expenses; and, 


WHEREAS, As per the sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, through the above 
said Show-Cause Notice, dated 20.10.2022, Mohd Israr was directed to submit his representation in writing with 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(iii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 6, 2023/वैशाख 16, 1945 147 


explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and to lodge account of election expenses within 20 days from the 
date of receipt of the notice; and, 


WHEREAS, the said notice was received by the candidate on 05.11.2022. The acknowledgment receipt has 
been submitted to the Commission by the District Election Officer, Moradabad, vide its letter no. 3886/29-34 


(वि.स.)/2022; and, 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Moradabad in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter No. 
3886/29-34(वि.स.)/2022 dated 06.12.2022 has reported that Mohd Israr has neither submitted any representation nor 


any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the due notice of the Election Commission of 
India, he has furnished neither any reason nor explanation for the said failure; and, 


WHEREAS, the Commission is satisfied that Mohd Israr has failed to lodge the account of election expenses 
and has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


i. has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


ii. has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order”; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Mohd Israr resident of Mohalla Saifiyan Agwanpur, Tehsil and 
District Moradabad a contesting candidate from 25-Kanth Assembly Constituency of the State of Uttar Pradesh in 
the General Election to the Legislative Assembly 2022 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member 
of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory 
for a period of three years from the date of this order. 


[No. 76/UP-LA/Moradabad/2022/CEMS-II] 
By Order, 
BINOD KUMAR, Secy.

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 2nd March, 2023 


O.N. 65.—WHEREAS, the General Election to 28-Moradabad Nagar Legislative Assembly of Uttar 
Pradesh, 2022 was announced vide Notification No. 48/61-2022 dated 21° J anuary, 2022. 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election has to, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge a true copy of the account of 
his election expenses with the District Election Officer; and, 


WHEREAS, the result of the said election along with 28-Moradabad Nagar Assembly Constituency was 
declared by the concerned Returning Officer on 107 March, 2022. Hence, the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 097 April, 2022; and, 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh and 
forwarded by the Joint Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh vide their letter No. 287/Nirvachan Vayy Cell/GE- 
LA/2022/Patra-01/2021, dated 27" April, 2021, Shri Vipin, a contesting candidate of Uttar Pradesh from 28- 
Moradabad Nagar Assembly Constituency of Uttar Pradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election expenses, in 
the manner, as required under law; and, 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the reports of the District Election Officer Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh and the 
Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, a Show-Cause notice, 76/UP-LA/2022/CEMS-III dated 20.10.2022 was issued 
under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Shri 
Vipin for not lodging the account of Election Expenses; and, 


WHEREAS, As per the sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, through the above 
said Show-Cause Notice, dated 20.10.2022, Shri Vipin was directed to submit his representation in writing with 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and to lodge account of election expenses within 20 days from the 
date of receipt of the notice; and, 


WHEREAS, the said notice was received by the candidate on 05.11.2022. The acknowledgment receipt has 
been submitted to the Commission by the District Election Officer, Moradabad, vide its letter no. 3886/29- 


34(वि.स.)/2022; and, 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Moradabad in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter No. 
3886/29-34(वि.स.)/2022 dated 06.12.2022 has reported that Shri Vipin has neither submitted any representation nor 


any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the due notice of the Election Commission of 
India, he has furnished neither any reason nor explanation for the said failure; and, 


WHEREAS, the Commission is satisfied that Shri Vipin has failed to lodge the account of election expenses 
and has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or 
under this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order”; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Shri Vipin resident of Kanoon Goyan, Muradabad a contesting 
candidate from 28-Moradabad Nagar Assembly Constituency of the State of Uttar Pradesh in the General Election to 
the Legislative Assembly 2022 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House of the 
Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three 
years from the date of this order. 


[No. 76/UP-LA/Moradabad/2022/CEMS-IIT] 
By Order, 
BINOD KUMAR, Secy.

New Delhi, the 2nd March, 2023 


O.N. 66.—WHEREAS, the General Election to 29-Kundarki Legislative Assembly of Uttar Pradesh, 2022 
was announced vide Notification No. 48/61-2022 dated 21“ January, 2022. 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at 
an election has to, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge a true copy of the account 
of his election expenses with the District Election Officer; and, 


WHEREAS, the result of the said election along with 29-Kundarki Assembly Constituency was declared 
by the concerned Returning Officer on 107 March, 2022. Hence, the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 097 April, 2022; and, 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh and 
forwarded by the Joint Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh vide their letter No. 287/Nirvachan Vayy Cell/GE- 
LA/2022/Patra-01/2021, dated 277 April, 2021, Smt. Daraksha Begum, a contesting candidate of Uttar Pradesh from 
29-Kundarki Assembly Constituency of Uttar Pradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election expenses, in the 
manner, as required under law; and, 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the reports of the District Election Officer Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh and the 
Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, a Show-Cause notice, 76/UP-LA/2022/CEMS-III dated 20.10.2022 was issued 
under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Smt. 
Daraksha Begum for not lodging the account of Election Expenses; and, 


WHEREAS, As per the sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, through the above 
said Show-Cause Notice, dated 20.10.2022, Smt. Daraksha Begum was directed to submit his representation in 
writing with explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and to lodge account of election expenses within 20 
days from the date of receipt of the notice; and, 


WHEREAS, the said notice was received by the candidate on 05.11.2022. The acknowledgment receipt has 
been submitted to the Commission by the District Election Officer, Moradabad, vide its letter no. 3886/29- 
34(वि.स.)/2022; and, 

WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Moradabad in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter No. 
3886/29-34(f4.4.)/2022 dated 06.12.2022 has reported that Smt. Daraksha Begum has neither submitted any 
representation nor any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the due notice of the 
Election Commission of India, he has furnished neither any reason nor explanation for the said failure; and, 


WHEREAS, the Commission is satisfied that Smt. Daraksha Begum has failed to lodge the account of 
election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or 
under this Act, and 


154 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 6, 2023/VAISAKHA 16, 1945 [PART II—SEC. 3(iii)] 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order”; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Smt. Daraksha Begum resident of Village Tewar Patti Urf 
Kazipura, Post Kundarki, Moradabad a contesting candidate from 29-Kundarki Assembly Constituency of the 
State of Uttar Pradesh in the General Election to the Legislative Assembly 2022 to be disqualified for being chosen as 
and for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a 
State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

New Delhi, the 16th March, 2023 


O.N. 68.—WHEREAS, the General Election to 170-Sarojini Nagar Legislative Assembly of Uttar Pradesh, 
2022 was announced vide Notification No. 68/61-2022 dated 27" January, 2022. 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at 
an election has to, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge a true copy of the account 
of his election expenses with the District Election Officer; and, 


WHEREAS, the result of the said election along with 170-Sarojini Nagar Assembly Constituency was 
declared by the concerned Returning Officer on 107 March, 2022. Hence, the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 097 April, 2022; and, 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh and 
forwarded by the Joint Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh vide their letter No. 287/Nirvachan Vayy Cell/GE- 
LA/2022/Patra-01/2021, dated 27" April, 2021, Shri Ramvaran Singh, a contesting candidate of Uttar Pradesh from 
170-Sarojini Nagar Assembly Constituency of Uttar Pradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election expenses, in 
the manner, as required under law; and, 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the reports of the District Election Office, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh and the 
Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, a Show-Cause notice, 76/UP-LA/2022/CEMS-III dated 29.11.2022 was issued 
under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Shri 
Ramvaran Singh for not lodging the account of Election Expenses; and, 


WHEREAS, As per the sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, through the above 
said Show-Cause Notice, dated 29.11.2022, Shri Ramvaran Singh was directed to submit his representation in 
writing with explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and to lodge account of election expenses within 20 
days from the date of receipt of the notice; and, 

WHEREAS, the said notice was received by the candidate on 22.12.2022. The acknowledgment receipt has 
been submitted to the Commission by the District Election Officer, Lucknow, vide its letter no. 139/निर्वाचन-8- 
219/2021-23; and, 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Lucknow in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter No. 


139/निर्वाचन-8-219/2021-23 dated 06.02.2023 has reported that Shri Ramvaran Singh has neither submitted any 


representation nor any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the due notice of the 
Election Commission of India, he has furnished neither any reason nor explanation for the said failure; and, 


WHEREAS, the Commission is satisfied that Shri Ramvaran Singh has failed to lodge the account of 
election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or 
under this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order”; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Shri Ramvaran Singh resident of Ward No. 18, Arya Nagar, Opp. 
Surya Galaxy Hotel, Shuklaganj, Unnao a contesting candidate from 170-Sarojini Nagar Assembly Constituency 
of the State of Uttar Pradesh in the General Election to the Legislative Assembly 2022 to be disqualified for being 
chosen as and for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative 
Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order. 


[No. 76/UP-LA/Lucknow/2022/CEMS-IT] 
By Order, 
BINOD KUMAR, Secy.

from 174-Lucknow Central Assembly Constituency of Uttar Pradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election

रहे हैं और उनके पास इस विफलता के लिए कोई भी उचितकारण अथवा औचित्य नहीं है; और

सभा के साधारण निर्वाचन, 2022 में निर्वाचन लड़ने वाले अभ्यर्थी सलमान सिद्दीकी निवासी 108/171, तालाब गगनी

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 23rd March, 2023 


O.N. 73.—WHEREAS, the General Election to 154-Sawayajpur Legislative Assembly of Uttar Pradesh, 
2022 was held vide Notification No. 68/61-2022 dated 27" January, 2022. 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at 
an election has to, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge a true copy of the account 
of his election expenses with the District Election Officer; and, 


WHEREAS, the result of the said election along with 154-Sawayajpur Assembly Constituency was 
declared by the concerned Returning Officer on 107 March, 2022. Hence, the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 097 April, 2022; and, 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Hardoi, Uttar Pradesh and 
forwarded by the Joint Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh vide their letter No. 287/Nirvachan Vayy Cell/GE- 
LA/2022/Patra-01/2021, dated 27" April, 2021, Lal Bahadur Singh, a contesting candidate of Uttar Pradesh from 
154-Sawayajpur Assembly Constituency of Uttar Pradesh, has failed to lodge account of his election expenses, in 
the manner, as required under law; and, 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the reports of the District Election Office, Hardoi, Uttar Pradesh and the Chief 
Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh, a Show-Cause notice, 76/UP-LA/2022/CEMS-III dated 13.12.2022 was issued under 
sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Lal Bahadur 
Singh for not lodging the account of Election Expenses; and, 


WHEREAS, As per the sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, through the above 
said Show-Cause Notice, dated 13.12.2022, Lal Bahadur Singh was directed to submit his representation in writing 
with explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and to lodge account of election expenses within 20 days from 
the date of receipt of the notice; and, 


WHEREAS, the said notice was received by the candidate on 17.01.2023. The acknowledgment receipt has 
been submitted to the Commission by the District Election Officer, Hardoi, vide its letter no. 


89/नि.व्यय.लेखा/वि.स.सा.नि./2022; and, 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Hardoi in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter No. 
89/नि.व्यय.लेखा/वि.स.सा.नि./2022 dated 28.02.2023 has reported that Lal Bahadur Singh has neither submitted any 


representation nor any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the due notice of the 
Election Commission of India, he has furnished neither any reason nor explanation for the said failure; and, 


WHEREAS, the Commission is satisfied that Lal Bahadur Singh has failed to lodge the account of election 
expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 


“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


170 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA: MAY 6, 2023/VAISAKHA 16, 1945 [PART II—SEC. 3(iii)] 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order”; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Lal Bahadur Singh resident of Gram - Goriya, Post — Aliganj 
Nankheriya, District- Hardoi a contesting candidate from 154-Sawayajpur Assembly Constituency of the State of 
Uttar Pradesh in the General Election to the Legislative Assembly 2022 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for 
being a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or 
Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order. 


[No. 76/UP-LA/Hardoi/2022/CEMS-II]]
